en.title: Brad Pitt Returns to Netflix as Cliff Booth in Tarantino's Next Movie
en.summary: Netflix is gearing up for a massive December 2026, promising some of its most anticipated releases of the year. From Quentin Tarantino's latest penned script to a bold reimagining of a literary classic, the streaming giant is pulling out all the stops.
en.body:
Netflix is setting the stage for a December 2026 that promises to be one of its biggest yet, with a slate of releases poised to dominate fan conversations. Leading the charge is **The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth**, a new film that sees **Brad Pitt** reprise his iconic role as the *Once Upon a Time in Hollywood* stuntman, with a script penned by **Quentin Tarantino** himself. This marks a significant cinematic event, bringing a beloved character and a legendary filmmaker's distinct voice to the streaming platform.

Beyond Tarantino's latest, December will also offer a fresh take on a literary titan with **Dolly Alderton**'s new adaptation of **Pride and Prejudice**. Fans of classic romance and sharp, modern storytelling will be eager to see how Alderton, known for her work on *Fleabag* and *The Pursuit of Love*, reimagines Jane Austen's enduring tale. The streamer is also leaning into true crime and animation, with **Melissa McCarthy** and **Clive Owen** starring in **The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey**, and **Brad Bird**'s animated feature **Ray Gunn** set to debut. Adding to the star power, **Cameron Diaz** will make an appearance in **Bad Day**.

The streaming giant isn't shying away from live events either, with a massive boxing match between **Tyson Fury** and **Anthony Joshua** on the cards, alongside a festive Christmas Day NFL doubleheader, signaling a broad entertainment strategy that spans scripted drama, comedy, animation, and live sports.

## Emily in Paris Bids Au Revoir

For fans of Parisian chic and soapy drama, the sixth and *final* season of **Emily in Paris** is set to premiere on December 24th. The beloved series, which has followed **Lily Collins**' titular character through her adventures in the City of Lights and beyond, will wrap up its run. Previous seasons have taken the production to stunning locales in France and Italy, and the conclusion is expected to bring back most of the core cast for a grand send-off, likely featuring new romantic entanglements and career triumphs for Emily.

## What Fans Are Saying

The December 2026 lineup has already generated significant buzz. The return of **Cliff Booth** is a particular point of excitement, with many speculating about Tarantino's signature dialogue and narrative style applied to further adventures of the character. The **Pride and Prejudice** adaptation is also a hot topic, with debates already forming about casting and the potential for a fresh, contemporary spin on Austen's beloved characters. The mix of original films, beloved series finales, and live sporting events suggests Netflix is aiming for a broad appeal, hoping to capture audiences during the holiday season with a diverse array of content.

## What's Next

As December 2026 approaches, Netflix will likely reveal more details about these upcoming projects, including trailers and specific release dates for individual episodes or films. Fans should keep an eye on the platform's official channels for further announcements regarding the final season of **Emily in Paris** and the much-anticipated **Cliff Booth** film.

content_raw: Pictures via Various Distributors Welcome to your very early look at everything coming to Netflix in the United States throughout December 2026! Netflix is closing out the year with some of its biggest titles of 2026, from a new David Fincher movie to live boxing and Christmas Day football. This month, all eyes are on  The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , with Brad Pitt back as the stuntman in a script by Quentin Tarantino, along with Dolly Alderton’s new take on  Pride and Prejudice . We’re also getting Melissa McCarthy and Clive Owen in  The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey , Brad Bird’s animated  Ray Gunn , Cameron Diaz in  Bad Day , and live events including Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua and a Christmas Day NFL doubleheader. Before we dig in, you can also keep track of every upcoming title on our  coming soon on Netflix calendar . What’s Coming to Netflix on December 1st Awake (2007)  – Hayden Christensen and Jessica Alba star in this thriller about a wealthy young man who remains conscious during heart surgery, and overhears a plot to kill him while unable to move or speak. Collect & Praise (Season 1) Netflix Original  – Druski stars in this semi-scripted comedy series about a money-driven megachurch pastor and his unpredictable deacon as they navigate scandal, chaos and controversy. Coyote Ugly (2000)  – Piper Perabo plays an aspiring songwriter who moves to New York City and finds work at a rowdy bar where the female staff dance on the counter. Also starring Maria Bello, Adam Garcia and Tyra Banks. Edward Scissorhands (1990)  – Tim Burton’s gothic fairy tale stars Johnny Depp as a gentle, unfinished artificial man with scissors for hands, who is taken in by a suburban family and falls for their daughter (Winona Ryder). Jão: Tales from the Void (Season 1) Netflix Original  – Brazilian documentary about the most intimate period in the career of singer Jão. Picture Credit: ABC Shifting Gears (Seasons 1-2)  – Tim Allen and Kat Dennings star in this ABC sitcom as a widowed classic car shop owner and his estranged daughter, who moves back in with her kids and forces the two to reconnect. The Good Liar (2019)  – Helen Mirren and Ian McKellen star in Bill Condon’s thriller about a career con man who sets his sights on a wealthy widow he meets online, only for the scheme to take some unexpected turns. The Kitchen (2019)  – Melissa McCarthy, Tiffany Haddish and Elisabeth Moss play three mob wives in 1970s Hell’s Kitchen who take over the family business after their husbands are sent to prison. Trinity (Season 1) Netflix Original – From Jed Mercurio (Bodyguard), this thriller stars Gugu Mbatha-Raw as Commander Katherine Decker, second-in-command of the nuclear submarine USS Kansas, whose involvement with US Secretary of Defense Webb Preston (Richard Madden) leads her to uncover a trail of secrets that may tie him to a global threat.
